questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if 

$$
{y}^{″}+4y=4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,y(0)=1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{″}+4y\} & =L\{4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\} \\ L\{{y}^{″}\}+4L\{y\} & =4L\{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce $L\{y\}=Y(s).$ 

To calculate $L\{{y}^{″}\},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a second derivative:

$$
L\{{y}^{″}\}={s}^{2}L\{y\}-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)
$$

Taking into account the given initial conditions, we get

$$
L\{{y}^{′}\}={s}^{2}Y(s)-s.
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L\{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}
$$

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{″}\}+4L\{y\} & =4L\{4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\} \\ ({s}^{2}Y(s)-s)+4Y(s) & =4(\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}) \\ ({s}^{2}+4)Y(s) & =s+\frac{4s}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ ({s}^{2}+4)Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{3}+8s}{{s}^{2}+4} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{s({s}^{2}+8)}{({s}^{2}+4)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if 

$$
{y}^{″}+2y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{″}+2y\} & =L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\} \\ L\{{y}^{″}\}+2L\{y\} & =L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's introduce $L\{y\}=Y(s).$ 

To calculate $L\{{y}^{″}\},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a second derivative:

$$
L\{{y}^{″}\}={s}^{2}L\{y\}-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)
$$

Taking into account the given initial conditions, we get

$$
L\{{y}^{″}\}={s}^{2}Y(s).
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\}=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{″}\}+2L\{y\} & =L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\} \\ {s}^{2}Y(s)+2Y(s) & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}+2)Y(s) & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)({s}^{2}+2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{″}+3{y}^{′}+y\} & =L\{3\operatorname{sin}⁡3\} \\ L\{{y}^{″}\}+3L\{{y}^{′}\}+L\{y\} & =3L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate $L\{{y}^{′}\}$ and $L\{{y}^{″}\},$  we use formulas for the Laplace transforms of the derivatives and apply the initial conditions:

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{′}\} & =sY(s)-y(0)=sY(s)+1 \\ L\{{y}^{″}\} & ={s}^{2}Y(s)-sy(0)-{y}^{′}(0)={s}^{2}Y(s)+s\end{aligned}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\}=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}
$$

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{″}\}+3L\{{y}^{′}\}+L\{y\} & =3L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\} \\ ({s}^{2}Y(s)+s)+3(sY(s)+1)+Y(s) & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}+3s+1)Y(s) & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+1}-s-3 \\ ({s}^{2}+3s+1)Y(s) & =\frac{3-{s}^{3}-s-3{s}^{2}-3}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}+3s+1)Y(s) & =-\frac{s({s}^{2}+3s+1)}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =-\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}-9y=-8{e}^{-t},\,y(0)=2,\,{y}^{′}(0)=2
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)-2s-2-9Y(s)=-\frac{8}{s+1}.
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)-2s-2-9Y(s) & =-\frac{8}{s+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-9)Y(s) & =2s+2-\frac{8}{s+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-9)Y(s) & =\frac{2({s}^{2}+2s-3)}{s+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-9)Y(s) & =\frac{2(s+3)(s-1)}{s+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{2(s+3)(s-1)}{(s+1)(s-3)(s+3)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{2(s-1)}{(s+1)(s-3)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{1}{s+1}+\frac{1}{s-3}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>3.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s+1}+\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\ y(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s+1}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-3}\} \\ y(t) & ={e}^{-t}+{e}^{3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}(t)-y(t)=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)=3
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)-3-Y(s)=-6(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}).
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)-3-Y(s) & =-6(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}) \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =3-\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ ({s}^{2}-1)Y(s) & =\frac{3({s}^{2}-1)}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>1.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+1}\} \\ y(t) & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$
